science.title: Quantitative relationship between coupled structural dynamics and collective order in the original Vicsek model
science.description: While the Vicsek model is widely used to understand active systems, the explicit relationship between structural evolution and the order transition remains an open question. Here we investigate this relationship in the original Vicsek system. We uncover a structure–order relationship across the investigated densities and noise strengths at fixed velocity and particle number, in which the polar order parameter exhibits a general correlation with the average interaction number. Furthermore, we reveal underlying structural self–similarities: cluster–level and system–level interaction number distributions show consistent normalized profiles, alongside a correlation between cluster size and orientation. Building on these correlations, we develop a phenomenological framework that quantitatively relates the order parameter to structural statistics. Moreover, over the investigated range of velocities, the structural features are maintained, whereas the structural–order correlation is augmented by a velocity factor. This work provides a structural perspective on the Vicsek model and suggests a quantitative relationship between microscopic structural organization and macroscopic collective behavior. We investigate the relationship between structural organization and collective order in the original Vicsek model. We uncover a universal structure–order relationship and develop a phenomenological framework linking microscopic structural statistics to macroscopic order, with velocity incorporated through an effective interaction number.

science.title: Nanoscale tech tracks proteins inside living neurons to guide Alzheimer's and Parkinson's drug discovery
science.description: A technology developed at The University of Queensland allowing scientists to observe how disease-related proteins behave inside living neurons will be used to advance early drug discovery for neurodegenerative diseases. The NASTIC (Nanoscale Spatiotemporal Indexing Clustering) platform, spun out into Brisbane-based startup Accretion Bio, enables researchers to study real-time biological processes in living cells across space and time at the single-molecule level for the first time.

science.title: Cortex-wide imaging in naturally behaving mice with 1-gram wireless mesoscopes
science.description: Revealing how distributed cortical circuits coordinate behavior in freely moving animals remains a central challenge in systems neuroscience, constrained by limited fields of view, low throughput, and the tethering required by current miniaturized microscopes1-4. Here, we present Airscope, a wireless mesoscope delivering 4 μm lateral resolution across a 6 mm field of view at 12.5 Hz, weighing 1.0 gram. An aspheric-lens design achieves a 2.84× shorter total track length than previous miniaturized microscopes1,2,5,6 while matching the neuron yield of benchtop one-photon mesoscopes; a tailored wireless link supports cable-free calcium imaging from >8,500 neurons per animal (25‑fold increase). Paired with a zero-shot behavior analyzer, Airscope enables cortical imaging across rich behavioral conditions, including room-scale enriched arenas, swimming assays, and multi-organ implantation, with concurrent recording from multiple animals. Using Airscope, we demonstrate versatile applications of untethered cortical imaging across diverse behavioral paradigms. We identify cortical activity patterns across multiple dorsal regions that correlate with behavioral signatures of social dominance, and show dorsal-cortical population activity prospectively decodes competition outcomes across paired animals. We observe reward-location-associated cortical activity patterns during maze exploration, and characterize Granger-causal influence from spinal cord to cortex during fear conditioning, enabled by simultaneous brain-spinal recordings. By uniting large-scale, cellular-resolution recording with unconstrained behavior, Airscope makes naturalistic, multi-animal cortical recording experimentally practical, and provides a broadly accessible technology for systems neuroscience.

science.description: Researchers discovered that recurring arthritis triggered by cancer immunotherapy may be driven by immune cells that remember previous attacks and return in a more aggressive state. The findings could pave the way for treatments that prevent painful flare-ups while preserving the immune system's ability to fight cancer.

science.title: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions
science.description: Monitoring large-scale neuronal activity in deep brain circuits is crucial for understanding the principles of brain function. However, existing large-scale cellular-resolution imaging techniques are limited in imaging depth and cannot monitor activity in areas deeper than the cortex in the intact brain. To address this challenge, we developed a Large Imaging Field of view Three-photon (LIFT) microscope with a FOV of  > 3 mm2. LIFT combines high-numerical-aperture optimized sampling, using a custom scanning module, with deep learning-based denoising, to enable population imaging in subcortical brain regions of mice and deep cortical regions of rats. We demonstrate calcium imaging in the intact mouse brain from more than 1500 cells across CA1, the surrounding white matter, and adjacent deep layers of the cortex, and show population imaging with high SNR at a depth of 1.2 mm in the rat cortex. The LIFT microscope offers versatility in imaging scale and rate and was built entirely from off-the-shelf components. Imaging large cell populations below the cortex in the intact brain is key for understanding brain function. LIFT, a multiscale three-photon microscope, tracks activity in over 1,500 cells across the hippocampus and adjacent regions in behaving mice.
